What if humans were the deadly, intelligent, predators in sci-fi movies?

I rather like the idea. My theory on why we have not been contacted boild down to just a handful of reasons, and I am 100% positive that one of these is the absolute truth:

  • We are alone. Harsh, terrifying, but possible.

  • The vastness of space is so....vast, that even if all of humanity collaborated, put aside war and racism and religion, money, politics, economics, all differences and hindrances and collaborated on the single most advanced computer and algorithm our great species could create - even that computer could not cope with the vastness of the universe - ergo, there could be interdimentional beings that have thousands of years yet before they even come close to discovering us. In other words, maybe there are multi-mullion planet civilizations out there, and even their collective is but a spec in an incomprehensibly vast sea of mostly nothing.

  • They are far more intelligent, and follow some sort of "Prime Directive" which does not include contacting a lesser species which has not discovered "FTL" (or whatever replacement tech)

  • Though they have FTL and mostly better tech and we do not, they see that we most certainly could have it within months if we tried. They have not developed weapons tech very far, nor do they have much combat experience, because the universe is mostly peaceful, and humanity is like a snarling, roaring, rabid lion, muscles rippling, claws tearing, throwing up dust and spittle and bits of it's own blood, and they are utterly terrified. They see that we are embroiled in our own affairs, too much to notice the presence of others in the universe (to their relief), and to intervene or introduce themselves would be to unleash a terrible, destructive, corrupt fury on the universe, the likes of which has never been seen in all the galaxies. The only hope is to remain hidden until the mealstrom calms.

I'm writing a book along the lines of my last point. Humanity does unite as one when contacted, but it's not a peaceful affair for the outsiders. We follow them to their homeworld, and completely erradicate their race as the rest of the galaxy looks on in sheer terror, watching as our unparralelled might descends upon the poor race that slipped up by saying hello. I think it's an interesting concept, the idea of humanity "growing up" after fucking up in public, rather than at home.

We are alone. Harsh, terrifying, but possible.

It's widely accepted that modern Humans have existed on Earth for about 200,000 years.
The Universe is approximately 13.8 billion years old.
That means we have existed for 0.000015% of the age of the Universe.

When one considers how vulnerable life is and how hostile the Universe is, it's entirely possible that many advanced civilizations have sprung up and died out before our Solar System even existed (About 4.5 billion years).

There could have been a civilization millions of years more advanced than ours, right next door on Mars and we wouldn't know.
Given how vast the Milky Way is, and how inconceivably vast the Universe is, we may never find any other life before we go extinct.

The chances of there being multiple forms of life in the same galactic neighbourhood at the same time are astronomically low, but it doesn't mean we are alone.
